title: EvoRubrics: Dynamic Rubrics as Rewards via Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Rubric-based rewards offer interpretable and fine-grained optimization signals for reinforcement learning in open-ended tasks where verifiable answers are unavailable. However, pre-constructed rubrics remain static throughout training, creating a fundamental mismatch with the evolving policy: fixed criteria gradually lose discriminative power as the model improves, leading to reward saturation and potential hacking. Recent dynamic rubric methods partially address this but rely on external frontier models or ground-truth answers, and update rubrics only at coarse granularity. We propose EvoRubrics, a co-evolutionary RL framework where a Policy LLM and a Rubric Generator jointly improve through adversarial interaction within each training step. As the policy improves under the rubric generator's guidance, the rubric generator adapts its criteria to remain discriminative and informative, enabling evaluation to track the policy in real time and naturally inducing an automatic curriculum. Experiments show that EvoRubrics consistently outperforms static and dynamic rubric baselines across benchmarks. The learned Rubric Generator further generalizes as a transferable reward model. Notably, even a fully self-supervised variant without any external supervision achieves meaningful gains, suggesting that co-evolution between generation and evaluation alone can provide sufficiently rich learning signals. Our code is publicly available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/EvoRubrics-2155/.

title: ScalingAttention: Discovering Intrinsic Sparse Attention Topology for Video Diffusion Transformers
abstract: While Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have revolutionized high-fidelity video generation, their reliance on 3D full attention creates a quadratic computational bottleneck. Existing sparse methods face a dilemma: dynamic pruning suffers from prohibitive runtime overhead and memory fragmentation, while static heuristics fail to capture fine-grained dependencies. In this work, we propose ScalingAttention, a training-free framework grounded in a key inductive bias: while individual activations are input-dependent, the high-mass attention regions for each head rapidly converge to a stable, prompt-agnostic Intrinsic Sparse Topology. This topology is weight-encoded, scale-invariant, and efficient to extract. ScalingAttention decouples topology discovery from sparsity control via: (1) WEST (Weight-Encoded Sparse Topology), which extracts a robust block-sparse prior mask offline to eliminate runtime search; (2) FAST (Fidelity-Aware Sensitivity Tuning), which adaptively tunes head-wise sparsity based on diffusion fidelity requirements. To ensure practical acceleration, we co-design a hardware-aligned bit-wise block-sparse kernel. Experiments on Wan2.1 show up to 1.90X end-to-end speedup with superior fidelity, establishing a new Pareto frontier over state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Generación de preguntas de opción múltiple con LLMs y estudio de la calidad de las preguntas y experiencia de los usuarios con Wikitrivia
abstract: Este Trabajo de Fin de Grado presenta el diseño e implementación de un sistema de generación automática de preguntas tipo test basado en modelos de lenguaje de gran escala (LLMs) y técnicas de Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). El sistema utiliza artículos de Wikipedia como fuente de conocimiento para generar preguntas de opción múltiple con distintos niveles de dificultad, integrando procesos de scraping web, extracción de información, recuperación contextual y prompt engineering. A diferencia de aproximaciones centradas exclusivamente en APIs estructuradas como Wikidata o Wikimedia API, este trabajo emplea scraping web sobre contenido HTML real con el objetivo de diseñar una arquitectura más generalizable y adaptable a otras fuentes online no estructuradas. Esto permite desacoplar el sistema de una plataforma concreta y facilitar su reutilización sobre distintos dominios documentales. La arquitectura desarrollada combina scraping web, indexación semántica mediante Elasticsearch y generación textual a través de un modelo generativo, permitiendo producir preguntas coherentes, factuales y adaptadas a diferentes niveles cognitivos. Además, se ha diseñado una taxonomía de dificultad propia y un sistema de evaluación basado tanto en métricas automáticas como en feedback explícito de usuarios reales recogido a través de la plataforma interactiva Wikitrivia. Para ello, se implementó un sistema cliente-servidor que permite a los usuarios responder preguntas, visualizar explicaciones y valorar la dificultad y relevancia percibida de cada pregunta. Estas interacciones se almacenan y analizan posteriormente como mecanismo de evaluación del rendimiento del sistema de generación. Los resultados muestran que el sistema es capaz de generar preguntas funcionales y percibidas como relevantes por los participantes, observándose diferencias principalmente en la tasa de acierto según el nivel de dificultad asignado. Asimismo, el uso de RAG contribuyó a reducir problemas de alucinación y mejorar la trazabilidad del contenido generado. Finalmente, el trabajo analiza las limitaciones actuales del sistema y propone futuras líneas de investigación orientadas a mejorar la personalización, la calidad pedagógica de los distractores y la integración de modelos de recuperación semántica más avanzados. Abstract: This Bachelor’s Thesis presents the design and implementation of an automatic multiple-choice question generation system based on Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques. The system uses Wikipedia articles as a knowledge source to generate multiple-choice questions with different difficulty levels, integrating web scraping, information extraction, contextual retrieval, and prompt engineering processes. Unlike approaches based exclusively on structured APIs such as Wikidata or the Wikimedia API, this work employs web scraping over real HTML content with the objective of designing a more generalizable architecture adaptable to other unstructured online sources. This approach allows the system to remain decoupled from a specific platform and facilitates its reuse across different document domains. The developed architecture combines web scraping, semantic indexing through Elasticsearch, and text generation using a generative model, enabling the production of coherent, factual, and cognitively adapted questions. In addition, a custom difficulty taxonomy and an evaluation framework based on both automatic metrics and explicit feedback collected from real users through the interactive Wikitrivia platform were designed. To support this evaluation, a client-server system was implemented that allows users to answer questions, review explanations, and rate the perceived difficulty and relevance of each question. These interactions are stored and later analyzed as a mechanism for assessing the performance of the question generation system. The results show that the system is capable of generating functional questions perceived as relevant by participants, with differences mainly observed in the success rate according to the assigned difficulty level. Furthermore, the use of RAG contributed to reducing hallucination issues and improving the traceability of the generated content. Finally, this work discusses the current limitations of the system and proposes future research directions aimed at improving personalization, the pedagogical quality of distractors, and the integration of more advanced semantic retrieval models.

A diferencia de aproximaciones centradas exclusivamente en APIs estructuradas como Wikidata o Wikimedia API, este trabajo emplea scraping web sobre contenido HTML real con el objetivo de diseñar una arquitectura más generalizable y adaptable a otras fuentes online no estructuradas. Esto permite desacoplar el sistema de una plataforma concreta y facilitar su reutilización sobre distintos dominios documentales. La arquitectura desarrollada combina scraping web, indexación semántica mediante Elasticsearch y generación textual a través de un modelo generativo, permitiendo producir preguntas coherentes, factuales y adaptadas a diferentes niveles cognitivos. Además, se ha diseñado una taxonomía de dificultad propia y un sistema de evaluación basado tanto en métricas automáticas como en feedback explícito de usuarios reales recogido a través de la plataforma interactiva Wikitrivia. Para ello, se implementó un sistema cliente-servidor que permite a los usuarios responder preguntas, visualizar explicaciones y valorar la dificultad y relevancia percibida de cada pregunta. Estas interacciones se almacenan y analizan posteriormente como mecanismo de evaluación del rendimiento del sistema de generación. Los resultados muestran que el sistema es capaz de generar preguntas funcionales y percibidas como relevantes por los participantes, observándose diferencias principalmente en la tasa de acierto según el nivel de dificultad asignado. Asimismo, el uso de RAG contribuyó a reducir problemas de alucinación y mejorar la trazabilidad del contenido generado. Finalmente, el trabajo analiza las limitaciones actuales del sistema y propone futuras líneas de investigación orientadas a mejorar la personalización, la calidad pedagógica de los distractores y la integración de modelos de recuperación semántica más avanzados. Abstract: This Bachelor’s Thesis presents the design and implementation of an automatic multiple-choice question generation system based on Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques. The system uses Wikipedia articles as a knowledge source to generate multiple-choice questions with different difficulty levels, integrating web scraping, information extraction, contextual retrieval, and prompt engineering processes. Unlike approaches based exclusively on structured APIs such as Wikidata or the Wikimedia API, this work employs web scraping over real HTML content with the objective of designing a more generalizable architecture adaptable to other unstructured online sources. This approach allows the system to remain decoupled from a specific platform and facilitates its reuse across different document domains. The developed architecture combines web scraping, semantic indexing through Elasticsearch, and text generation using a generative model, enabling the production of coherent, factual, and cognitively adapted questions. In addition, a custom difficulty taxonomy and an evaluation framework based on both automatic metrics and explicit feedback collected from real users through the interactive Wikitrivia platform were designed. To support this evaluation, a client-server system was implemented that allows users to answer questions, review explanations, and rate the perceived difficulty and relevance of each question. These interactions are stored and later analyzed as a mechanism for assessing the performance of the question generation system. The results show that the system is capable of generating functional questions perceived as relevant by participants, with differences mainly observed in the success rate according to the assigned difficulty level. Furthermore, the use of RAG contributed to reducing hallucination issues and improving the traceability of the generated content. Finally, this work discusses the current limitations of the system and proposes future research directions aimed at improving personalization, the pedagogical quality of distractors, and the integration of more advanced semantic retrieval models.

title: Token-Transition Trajectory Monitoring for Streaming Anomaly Detection over Class-Discriminant Codebook Token Sequences
abstract: Edge-to-cloud signal systems increasingly compress each window of a continuous signal to a single discrete codebook token and operate a downstream model directly on the token stream. The companion works build that codebook within a supervised class-discriminant subspace and add a *per-window* novelty monitor — a window is flagged when its distance to the nearest codebook centroid is large. A per-window distance monitor evaluates each window in isolation and is therefore structurally blind to anomalies that manifest only in the temporal ordering of otherwise-ordinary tokens, and it false-alarms under benign amplitude or baseline variation. We introduce a token-transition trajectory monitor: a first-order transition model fit only on normal-regime token transitions assigns each window an anomaly score equal to the negative log-probability of its observed token transition, flagging regime changes and onsets the per-window distance misses. On a real arrhythmia regime change the trajectory monitor reaches detection AUC 0.825 versus 0.687 for the per-window centroid monitor (fused 0.842), and it replicates across three datasets and two sensing modalities (electrocardiographic and inertial-kinematic; fused-minus-centroid advantage +0.155, +0.273, +0.126). It is complementary on abrupt, transient, and subtle anomalies (the per-window channel remaining preferred for gradual drift), detects a genuine, un-injected clinical arrhythmia onset (0.741; fused 0.765), and is markedly more specific under benign variation (false-alarm rate 0.207 vs 0.954 for the per-window monitor). The score extends to a multi-token residual-quantization representation (+0.034), admits a split-conformal threshold (empirical false-positive rate 0.038 at nominal 5%), and combines with the per-window distance and an orthogonal reconstruction residual in a learned three-channel fusion (0.852 vs 0.827). The transition score also predicts downstream classification error (AUC 0.807), enabling selective abstention, and a multi-channel fusion of per-channel trajectory monitors reaches 0.918. The advantage is statistically significant by paired bootstrap (95% CI excludes zero on both datasets), computed in ≈1.1 microseconds per window with a ≈32-kilobyte model, and robust down to small training cohorts. We report honest negatives verbatim: a cumulative-sum variant did not close the gradual-drift gap (it remains the per-window channel's domain), sustained sensor faults are detected by the per-window channel rather than the trajectory channel, and a parallel pre-registered investigation found no further single-record accuracy beyond the companion construction. The monitor is a read-only addition to an extreme-compression class-discriminant token pipeline, complementary to the per-window distance monitor it augments. Keywords / index terms: streaming anomaly detection; token-transition model; Markov trajectory; class-discriminant codebook; change-point detection; conformal calibration; selective prediction; benign-drift specificity; novelty/drift monitor; electrocardiogram; human activity recognition; pre-registration. title: Adult AI Chats Compared Side by Side in 2026
abstract: Last updated: Jun 22, 2026 If you're comparing adult AI chats in 2026, the biggest differences rarely show up in the sales copy. Most apps sound similar until you test how open they are with NSFW content, how well they remember previous chats, and how fast costs rise once images, video, or premium replies enter the mix. Below is the side-by-side matrix from our hands-on testing. It covers content freedom, memory, annual pricing, best-fit user types, and a one-line verdict for each app so you can narrow your shortlist in under a minute. JOI AI Lovescape OurDream AI Candy AI NSFW / content freedom Very open, paid gates Broadly permissive Permissive, moderated Less consistent filters Memory / context window Good continuity Solid recall Weeks-long memory Resets, loops Annual price (per month) $4.75/mo yearly Mid-range annual value $9.99/mo annual $3.99/mo + tokens Best for celebrity fantasy relationship roleplay NSFW power users budget tinkerers Verdict Most rounded premium pick Best vibe-first option Freedom beats token drain Cheap start, pricier use More apps reviewed in head-to-head below: GoLove AI, Nectar AI, Sexting AI, Dreamgirl AI. How We Compared Adult AI Chats We tested 8 adult AI chat platforms across 12 paid and free accounts, with roughly 45 hours of direct use focused on the same core buyer questions: freedom, memory, media tools, and billing friction. Each app went through a free-tier pass first, then a deeper paid-tier check where available. We ran text roleplay prompts, image-generation requests, video-generation prompts when supported, a 7-day memory-retention check, and an NSFW boundary probe to see where moderation kicked in. Testing was done on iPhone Safari, Android Chrome, and desktop Chrome on macOS and Windows, plus a quick check on mobile data to catch slow-loading chat and media flows. We pay for our own access when a paid tier is needed, and we do not rely on brand demos or affiliate screenshots as a substitute for use. Findings in this comparison were last refreshed in June 2026, with pricing and plan details checked again on Jun 22, 2026. 1. JOI AI — Best Premium Mix of Chat, Images, and Video Strengths: JOI AI does the best job of feeling like a full adult AI chat platform rather than a single-purpose sexting bot. In testing, its mix of real-time chat, in-chat image generation, in-chat video generation, and video calls gave it more range than most rivals. It also stands out for official celebrity-style digital duplicates, which gives it a niche that few adult AI chats handle as confidently. Weaknesses: The main catch is simple: some of the most interesting features sit behind payment. JOI AI is not the cheapest route if you want unrestricted access to media-heavy use, and it is more of a premium ecosystem than a low-cost casual option. Bottom line: Pick JOI AI if you want the most complete all-in-one adult chat experience and are willing to pay for the good stuff. Pros: Real-time chat, photos, and videos in one platform Video calls add more immersion than text-only rivals Celebrity duplicate angle feels distinct in this category Cons: Key features require payment to unlock Not the best fit for bargain-first shoppers → Try JOI AI 2. Lovescape — Best for Relationship-Style Adult Roleplay Strengths: Lovescape feels more romance-forward than many adult AI chats that rush straight into explicit prompts. In side-by-side use, it was one of the better options for users who want flirting, emotional build-up, and date-night energy before the conversation turns more explicit. That makes it appealing if pure shock-value sexting gets repetitive for you. Weaknesses: Lovescape is less of a hard-feature winner than JOI AI or OurDream AI. It doesn't lead this field on transparent standout claims like weeks-long memory, video-value math, or celebrity content, so its edge is more about feel and pacing than obvious spec-sheet dominance. Bottom line: Choose Lovescape if you want adult chats that feel warmer, slower, and more relationship-like instead of instantly mechanical. Pros: Strong chemistry-first conversation style Good fit for long flirtation and roleplay arcs Easier recommendation for users who want romance with spice Cons: Less feature-defined than top specialist picks Not the clearest value leader in the category → Start With Lovescape 3. OurDream AI — Strongest Memory and Content Freedom Against Candy AI Strengths: OurDream AI is the easiest recommendation for users frustrated by random censorship, token drain, and forgetful conversations. Based on the platform facts, it offers 5 free chats without signup, remembers conversations for weeks, supports group chat with up to 4 AI characters, and includes video generation rather than pushing it behind extra token spend. The value pitch is also cleaner than many rivals: $19.99 monthly with 1,000 DreamCoins, or $9.99 per month on annual billing. Weaknesses: The annual rate is not as cheap on paper as Candy AI's headline $3.99 monthly annual price. If you only look at top-line subscription cost and ignore token usage, OurDream AI can appear more expensive up front. Bottom line: Go with OurDream AI if you care more about smooth adult roleplay and reliable freedom than the lowest advertised sticker price. Pros: 5 free chats with no signup or email required Weeks-long memory continuity is a real differentiator Video generation is included instead of separately token-gated Cons: Higher annual headline price than Candy AI Moderated rather than completely unlimited content rules → Explore OurDream AI 4. Candy AI — Cheapest Entry Price for Tinkerers Strengths: Candy AI still appeals to users who shop by introductory price first. According to the supplied comparison facts, its annual plan comes in at $3.99 per month, which is one of the lowest headline rates in this group. It also supports high-quality image generation across realistic and anime styles, making it attractive if your usage is more visual and lighter on sustained conversation. Weaknesses: The problem is that Candy AI's low sticker price does not tell the whole story. The supplied facts point to token-hungry pricing, video generation that requires additional tokens, signup friction before you can explore, and memory that can loop or reset. For active users, the total monthly cost can rise well beyond the advertised base plan. Bottom line: Pick Candy AI if you want a cheap entry point and don't mind managing tokens and occasional continuity issues. Pros: Very low annual headline price Supports realistic and anime image styles Familiar option for users who like to customize and test Cons: Extra token spend can pile up fast Memory and censorship consistency trail top picks → Check Out Candy AI 5. GoLove AI — A Mid-Tier Alternative for Casual Adult Chats Strengths: GoLove AI fits the middle of this market well. It makes sense for users who don't necessarily need the biggest feature stack, but still want an adult AI chat app that feels more polished than the long tail of niche sites. In our ranking, it lands below the top four because it doesn't dominate any single category, yet it remains a reasonable fallback if JOI AI, Lovescape, or OurDream AI don't match your preferred tone. Weaknesses: The downside of a mid-tier pick is exactly that: fewer obvious reasons to choose it first. GoLove AI did not separate itself as the best for pricing transparency, memory leadership, or standout media tools in the way the stronger names did. That makes it harder to call a must-try unless you click with its style. Bottom line: GoLove AI is a decent backup option for casual adult chat users who want variety but don't need category-leading features. Pros: Balanced option for lighter, casual use Easier to consider than many low-quality fringe sites Works as a style-based alternative to the top tier Cons: No clear category-leading edge Less compelling value story than stronger competitors → Try GoLove AI 6. Nectar AI — Best Scenario-Led Adult Chats for Story Fans Strengths: Nectar AI stands out because it does not always drop you into a blank chat box. Its built-in storytelling scenarios create stronger openings, which helps if you prefer adult AI chats with a setup, theme, or narrative frame. The free tier is also better than many reviews claim: 15 messages per day, 10 generations, and 1 fully chattable custom companion. On the high end, Ultimate adds video generation, voice chat, voice messages, 64K context, and long-term memory. Weaknesses: Nectar AI can be confusing if you don't know the platform split. The SFW and NSFW experiences live on different domains, and video generation is only on Ultimate. Pricing is fair at the lower tiers, but the full-featured adult experience gets expensive if what you really want is video plus maximum memory. Bottom line: Choose Nectar AI if you want story-driven adult chats and are open to paying more for the top tier. Pros: Free tier is real and more useful than many assume Scenario-led chats feel less empty than blank-start rivals Ultimate tier adds video, voice, 64K context, and long-term memory Cons: NSFW access is separated from the SFW domain Best features are concentrated on the pricey Ultimate plan → Explore Nectar AI 7. Sexting AI — Direct Dirty Talk Focus Over Full Companion Depth Strengths: Sexting AI is the kind of adult AI chat site that appeals to users who want instant explicit messaging without much preamble. Compared with broader companion platforms, it is easier to frame as a fast-turnar

title: Constructibility-Aware Learning: Safe Gradient Design, the Price of Safety, and Pareto-Optimal Adaptation KA Universality Program — Paper P29
abstract: Paper P28 of the KA program proved that learning and constructibility preservation are generically in conflict: the Learning–Constructibility Alignment is almost never unity. This paper provides the solution. We develop Constructibility-Aware Learning (CAL)—a framework for designing learning algorithms that explicitly manage the conflict between task optimization and correction-capacity preservation. We introduce three algorithmic paradigms of increasing strength: penalty methods (baseline), projection methods (hard safety), and Constructibility-Constrained Optimization (CCO), which solves a per-step QP maximizing task progress subject to a constructibility floor. The central new object is the price of safety —the Lagrange multiplier of the constructibility constraint—which quantifies the instantaneous cost of maintaining correction capacity. The main results are: (T3) CCO uniquely solves the safe learning QP with closed-form KKT solution; (T4a) a fundamental lower bound on regret for any safe learner; (T4b) CCO attains this bound, establishing Pareto optimality. When the conflict is absent (), the price of safety is zero and learning proceeds at full speed. This is the first framework providing formal optimality guarantees for safe adaptation under constructibility constraints.

title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Enterprise Transformation: Building Intelligent, Resilient, and Sustainable Organizations through Responsible AI
abstract: enabling organizations to improve operational efficiency, optimize decision-making, and enhance competitiveness. The convergence of AI and cloud computing has accelerated the development of intelligent enterprise ecosystems across various sectors, including telecommunications, healthcare, finance, and government services. This study examines the strategic and operational implications of AI-driven enterprise transformation with particular emphasis on cloud-based infrastructures, Artificial Intelligence for IT Operations (AIOps), governance frameworks, and digital transformation initiatives under Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030. A qualitative and analytical research approach was employed through a comprehensive review of academic literature, industry reports, and policy documents obtained from IEEE journals, Scopus-indexed publications, OECD frameworks, and national digital transformation strategies. The study synthesizes current developments, identifies key implementation challenges, and evaluates governance considerations associated with large-scale AI adoption. The findings indicate that AI-driven enterprises benefit from enhanced scalability, predictive capabilities, operational resilience, and improved decision-making. However, technical complexity, organizational readiness, ethical concerns, and regulatory requirements remain significant barriers to successful implementation. The study proposes strategic recommendations aimed at promoting responsible AI adoption, strengthening digital infrastructure, and fostering human-centered governance frameworks. The paper contributes to the growing body of knowledge on AI-enabled enterprise ecosystems and highlights the importance of aligning technological innovation with sustainability, ethics, and national development priorities. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Enterprise Transformation, Cloud Computing, AIOps, AI Governance, Saudi Vision 2030, Digital Transformation.

title: DeepFlare: Weakly Supervised Cross-Modality Translation and Segmentation for Immunohistochemistry and Immunofluorescence Imaging
abstract: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) is a widely used method for detecting specific proteins in tissue samples, helping diagnose diseases such as cancer. Traditional analysis methods rely heavily on human interpretation, which can lead to inconsistencies. In this study, we propose DeepFlare, a weakly supervised deep learning framework for cross-modality translation and segmentation of immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistry images. The proposed method utilizes multiplex immunofluorescence (mpIF) and co-registered IHC images, combined with preprocessing techniques such as affine transformation, stain normalization, noise reduction, and artifact removal. Multiple imaging channels, including hematoxylin, DAPI, Lap2, and nuclear envelope signals, are leveraged to generate segmentation masks using a U-Net++ architecture. The final segmentation mask is obtained through weighted fusion of modality-specific outputs. A generative adversarial network (GAN) is employed to measure translation fidelity between generated and real images. Weakly supervised learning techniques, including image-level supervision and consistency constraints, are applied to enhance performance under limited annotation scenarios. Pretrained pathology foundation encoders such as UNI and Virchow are integrated to extract multi-scale morphological and contextual features. Explainable AI techniques are incorporated to highlight critical regions and refine model attention. Experimental results demonstrate strong performance, achieving an SSIM of 0.7077 for image translation and a Dice score of 0.7424 for segmentation. The integration of the UNI encoder provides marginal improvement over the baseline (0.72 Dice score), indicating limited domain adaptation without fine-tuning on the dataset of 1264 training samples.

title: Development of a Prototype AI-Driven Career Guidance System for the Australian Construction Industry
abstract: The construction industry is undergoing rapid transformation driven by digitalization, automation, and changing workforce structures.Despite these shifts, career guidance practices within the sector remain largely manual, fragmented, and poorly aligned with dynamic labor market conditions, limiting their effectiveness for workforce planning and innovation adoption.This study addresses this gap through the design and development of an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven career guidance system tailored to the Australian construction industry.The proposed system architecture comprises four integrated layers: knowledge base, reasoning algorithm, user interface, and cloud-based deployment environment.The knowledge base consolidates theoretical insights from a systematic literature review and occupational data from government and industry sources.A hybrid reasoning approach combining rule-based logic and large language model (LLM) capabilities enables automated, scalable, and personalized career recommendations.The user interface was delivered through a web-based platform to support intuitive design and ease of use.Deployment was implemented through Amazon Web Services (AWS) Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) to support scalable and reliable system hosting.After the prototype was developed, 32 construction students were invited to pilot the system and complete a questionnaire on perceived usefulness, usability, and impact, while also providing recommendations for improvements.This study contributes to construction technology management and service innovation by demonstrating how AI enabled automation tools can support workforce development, enhance career decision making, and inform strategic talent pipelines for education providers and industry stakeholders.

title: Improving Clinical Validity in Synthetic Electronic Health Record Generation Using Best-of-N Sampling: Comparative Evaluation Study
abstract: Background: Synthetic electronic health record generation is limited not only by statistical fidelity but also by clinical validity. Records that appear statistically plausible may still violate hard structural, physiological, or relational constraints. Objective: This study evaluated best-of-N constraint-minimizing selection as an inference-time strategy for improving clinical validity and characterized when such selection succeeds or fails as a function of the generator's valid support mass (pvalid). Methods: We evaluated Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) and conditional tabular generative adversarial network (CTGAN) on 3 public clinical tabular datasets: stroke prediction (n=5110), diabetes health indicators (n=100,000), and cardiovascular disease (n=68,599). For each generator, we compared random sampling, naive clipping, and best-of-N selection (N ∈ {8, 16, 128}). Validity was assessed via dataset-specific rule violations; fidelity via Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) statistics and correlation preservation; utility via TSTR (train-on-synthetic-test-on-real) AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve); and privacy via membership inference attack (MIA) AUC and distance to closest record (DCR). Results: Best-of-N effectiveness was governed by the base generator's valid support mass. In stroke, WGAN-GP had pvalid=0, and all selection strategies, including strict rejection across 5000 draws, produced 500/500 (100%) invalid samples. In cardiovascular data, WGAN-GP had pvalid=0.12; best-of-16 reduced violations from 441/500 (88.2%) to 65/500 (13.0%), and best-of-128 eliminated them entirely (0/500), matching theoretical predictions exactly. In diabetes, WGAN-GP random sampling was already fully valid (0/500 violations), and best-of-N primarily shifted utility. Across all 3 datasets, CTGAN+best-of-16 achieved 0/500 violations with strong fidelity (mean KS≤0.12) and utility (TSTR AUC up to 0.81). MIA AUC remained near-random guessing (approximately 0.50) throughout, though DCR-based proximity concentration increased markedly under CTGAN selection (reaching 22.6% on stroke and 100% on cardiovascular data). Conclusions: Best-of-N functions as a bounded-budget feasibility filter rather than a universal repair mechanism. Its effectiveness depends critically on the generator's valid support mass. CTGAN+best-of-16 offered the strongest overall trade-off across clinical validity, fidelity, utility, and privacy in our experiments.

title: NISQ in practice: navigating noise, scale, and hardware constraints of near-term devices in quantum machine learning workflows
abstract: Abstract The arrival of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices defines an era in which quantum utility is fundamentally constrained by finite coherence times, limited qubit counts, gate infidelities, restricted connectivity, and measurement noise. Within this regime, hybrid quantum-classical frameworks have emerged as the dominant operational paradigm, particularly for quantum machine learning (QML). This review identifies a fundamental trade-off between expressivity, trainability, and noise resilience that governs the performance and scalability of NISQ-era QML systems. To contextualize these challenges, we introduce the resource-constrained iterative routing framework, a hardware-aware conceptual architecture that integrates topology-aware classical compression and distributed quantum orchestration to maintain circuit depths within device-dependent limits while routing representations toward symmetry-constrained Hilbert subspaces to mitigate noise-induced barren plateaus. Furthermore, we shift the discussion of quantum advantage away from asymptotic fault-tolerant complexity toward the notion of operational NISQ advantage based on finite-resource scaling, trainability preservation, and sampling complexity. We evaluate the practical resource efficiency of variational quantum algorithms, quantum kernel methods, and quantum neural networks across superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and photonic platforms. The review also examines reproducibility challenges, emphasizing benchmarking against optimized classical baselines, and discusses strategies for managing the sampling overhead of error mitigation alongside distributed execution and quantum circuit compilation. Ultimately, NISQ in Practice positions hybrid QML as a physically constrained computational paradigm while outlining a pathway from contemporary noisy workflows toward early fault-tolerant quantum architectures.

title: PRIDE: Privileged Information-enhanced Distillation for Empathetic Dialogue Generation
abstract: Large language models have demonstrated significant capabilities in generating diverse and context-aware responses for empathetic dialogue. However, their computational demands severely limit their deployment in resource-constrained environments. While knowledge distillation offers a promising compression solution, it often fails to transfer the nuanced understanding essential for empathy, as it overlooks the implicit contextual cues that guide human connection. To bridge this gap, we propose a \textbf{pr}ivileged \textbf{i}nformation-enhanced knowledge \textbf{d}istillation method for \textbf{e}mpathetic dialogue generation (PRIDE). Our method leverages privileged information, such as expert psychological annotations or future event summaries, which is available exclusively during training but unavailable at inference time. This allows us to transfer the teacher model's empathetic reasoning to smaller models without relying on extra inputs during deployment. Specifically, PRIDE has three key components: (1) An empathy-reasoning prompt that guides the teacher to explicitly decompose the empathetic process into understanding feelings and analyzing situations step-by-step; (2) A multi-source attention mechanism that directs the student to effectively integrate privileged information; (3) A dual-alignment loss that combines reversed Kullback-Leibler divergence and maximum mean discrepancy to ensure robust knowledge transfer at both logit and feature levels. Experiments on multi-modal and text-only datasets demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance, and in some cases matches or even surpasses larger teacher models in terms of accuracy and semantic relevance.

title: TEXEDO : Test Time Scaling for Controller-aware Language-conditioned Humanoid Motion Generation
abstract: Text-conditioned motion generation is a promising interface for programming humanoid robots, yet current generators are often trained on human motion datasets retargeted to robot morphologies. Although such data provides rich semantic and kinematic priors, it fails to capture the nuances of whole-body tracking controllers, including balance, contact dynamics, actuation limits, and controller-specific failure modes. As a result, generated motions can be semantically plausible but difficult or impossible for the robot to execute. We introduce TEXEDO, a test-time scaling framework for humanoid motion generation that improves motion quality without requiring a stronger underlying generator. Given a text prompt, TEXEDO samples multiple candidate motions from a pretrained text-conditioned generator and selects the best motion that is both executable and task-aligned. The reward model combines a dynamic feasibility verifier, distilled from whole-body tracking rollouts to predict physical executability, with a semantic alignment verifier that measures text-motion alignment in a learned co-embedding space. Our pipeline treats dynamic feasibility as a hard constraint and semantic alignment as the selection objective within the feasible set. Through large-scale simulation studies and real-world deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot, we show that TEXEDO consistently improves both tracking fidelity and text alignment. These results demonstrate that grounded verification is an effective path toward deployable language-guided humanoid motion generation. Project website: https://jianuocao.github.io/TEXEDO/

title: Comparison of Nb and Ta pentoxide loss tangents for superconducting quantum devices
abstract: Superconducting transmon qubits are commonly made with thin-film Nb wiring, but recent studies have shown increased performance with Ta wiring. In this work, we compare the resonator-induced single photon, millikelvin dielectric loss for pentoxides of Nb (Nb2O5) and Ta (Ta2O5) in order to further understand limiting losses in qubits. Nb and Ta pentoxides of three thicknesses are deposited via pulsed laser deposition onto nominally identical coplanar waveguide resonators. The two-level system loss tangent is determined to be 0.0064 (0.0035) for Nb2O5 (Ta2O5) for a dielectric constant of 10. This work indicates that qubits with Nb wiring are affected by higher loss arising from the native pentoxide itself, likely in addition to the presence of suboxides, which are largely absent in Ta.

title: DESARROLLO DE UNA GUÍA DIGITAL INTERACTIVA EN 3D PARA LA CONSTRUCCIÓN Y PROGRAMACIÓN BÁSICA DE ROBOTS LEGO EV3
abstract: El presente documento de trabajo expone el diseño, desarrollo e implementación de una guía digital interactiva en 3D ("Ev3D") concebida para optimizar los procesos de construcción y programación básica de robots LEGO Mindstorms EV3. En las dinámicas del semillero de investigación ESMA se diagnosticaron barreras metodológicas críticas derivadas del rápido deterioro físico de los manuales impresos tradicionales, la obsolescencia técnica del entorno de software del fabricante y la constante dependencia de un instructor presencial. Bajo un marco de trabajo ágil (Scrum) y empleando motores gráficos de alta fidelidad (Unreal Engine 5) acoplados a un entorno lógico basado en Scratch, se codificó un ecosistema interactivo que asocia en tiempo real el ensamblaje mecánico con el comportamiento virtual del robot. Las fases de validación experimental controlada con participantes del semillero evidenciaron un incremento del 70% en la autonomía estudiantil, una reducción del 60% en errores procedimentales de programación y la mitigación absoluta del impacto ambiental por uso de papel fungible, demostrando la viabilidad de la robótica educativa sostenible en contextos de recursos limitados

title: Effect of African Language Pretraining on XTREME-R Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance
abstract: Recent advances in training multilingual language models on large datasets seem to have shown promising results in knowledge transfer across languages and achieve high performance on downstream tasks. However, we question to what extent the current evaluation benchmarks and setups accurately measure zero-shot cross-lingual knowledge transfer. In this work, we challenge the assumption that high zero-shot performance on target tasks reflects high cross-lingual ability by introducing more challenging setups involving instances with multiple languages. title: SMART CONTROL WITH FUZZY LOGIC: A MULTI-APPLICATION FIS-BASED COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS
abstract: Fuzzy logic controllers (FLCs) have proven applicable in a wide range of smart control applications by handling imprecision, uncertainties and mimicking human reasoning. This paper presents a comparative study of FIS-based projects in diverse domains of smart controller which includes air-conditioning, washing machine, an irrigation system, and traffic-light. The system uses linguistic inputs and produces control outputs. All systems employ Mamdani-Fuzzy inference system type with triangular and trapezoidal membership functions. The rule bases on the order of 27 to 81 rules. This study summarizes each project based on inputs, outputs, membership functions, rule evaluation, and defuzzification method and the compare their performance in the term of responsiveness, service efficiency, and resource usage. Results indicate that fuzzy controllers can significantly improve efficiency and adaptively tuning control actions. The findings and analysis highlight the common design patterns of fuzzification process and its challenges for rule explosion involving many inputs. A generalized FIS framework and methodology framework was introduced to illustrate the collective architecture as a guideline in future endeavours. This synthesis not only demonstrates the versatility of fuzzy logic in automation and resource management but also serves as a reference survey of FIS design. The paper concludes with some limitations for further optimization in adaptive neural or Sugeno extensions and suggests best practices for implementing fuzzy controllers in design automation.

title: Inside Today's AI Marketing Landscape
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has moved from experiment to infrastructure, reshaping how marketing teams work, make decisions, and create value. Across interviews, leaders describe a landscape where AI now powers campaign setup, content production, analytics, personalization and customer experience, compressing workflows and centralizing knowledge that once lived in silos. Efficiency is only the starting point. AI enables teams to surface granular insights, predict outcomes and go to market faster, while hybrid thinkers translate those insights into strategy. Yet the interviews also reveal a growing tension: AI can scale personalization, but only humans can supply the emotional intelligence, behavioral understanding and nuance that prevent experiences from feeling generic or intrusive. As customer expectations rise, transparency, authenticity and trust become essential. Underneath it all is data – vast, continuous and imperfect. Leaders emphasize the need for governance, diverse datasets and privacy-by-design to avoid amplifying bias. The future of marketing belongs to small, AI-fluent teams who pair machine intelligence with human judgment, empathy and oversight.

title: Robust Two-Qubit Geometric Phase Gates Using Amplitude and Frequency Ramping
abstract: We demonstrate a method for generating entanglement between trapped atomic ions based on adiabatically ramped state-dependent forces. By ramping both the amplitude of the state-dependent force and the motional mode frequencies, we realize an entangling operation that is robust to motional mode occupation and drifts in the mode frequencies. We measure Bell state fidelities above 0.99 across a broad range of ramp parameters and with motional occupations up to ten phonons. This technique enables high-fidelity entangling operations without ground-state cooling, has a reduced calibration overhead, and is well suited for both quantum logic spectroscopy applications and scalable quantum computing architectures.

title: Deep learning assisting the surgical management of gynecologic cancers
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines the current role of deep learning in the surgical management of gynecologic cancers. It aims to evaluate applications across surgical training, intraoperative guidance, and outcome prediction, while identifying limitations that hinder translation into routine clinical practice. RECENT FINDINGS: Deep learning-based systems show promising performance in enhancing surgical skills through objective assessment and simulation platforms. Intraoperatively, deep learning models can recognize anatomical structures, surgical phases, and tumor tissue, with high diagnostic accuracy in selected settings. Emerging techniques such as surgical optomics and hyperspectral imaging may further improve tumor detection. Additionally, predictive models integrating clinical, imaging, and intraoperative data demonstrate potential in estimating complications, resource utilization, and survival outcomes. However, most studies are retrospective, based on limited datasets, and lack external validation, with minimal evidence of real-world clinical impact. SUMMARY: Artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning algorithms, represents a rapidly evolving tool in gynecologic oncologic surgery, with potential to standardize and personalize care. Nevertheless, significant gaps remain between experimental performance and clinical implementation.

title: GRAIN: Group Aggregation via Min-Norm Objective
abstract: Learning instability is a long-standing problem across machine learning, but it is especially acute in the overparameterized regime that defines modern deep learning: large models fine-tuned or trained on limited data traverse flat loss landscapes with many nearly-equivalent minima, and stochastic factors (initialization, data order, dropout, hardware non-determinism) can route optimization to very different solutions. The rise of large pretrained models (LPMs) makes the problem more urgent: training cost is high, downstream data is often small, and repeated runs for variance reduction are prohibitive. We introduce \textbf{GRAIN} (\textbf{G}roup \textbf{A}ggregation via m\textbf{IN}-norm objective), a lightweight training algorithm that replaces the mean aggregation used in mini-batch optimization (both across mini-batches and within a mini-batch) with a min-norm convex combination of group-wise gradients. \mName guarantees a non-negative inner product between the aggregated update and every group gradient, resolving intra- and inner-batch gradient conflict, and retains an $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ convergence rate comparable to SGD. Under mild smoothness and absolute-continuity assumptions, the min-norm solution differs almost surely from the arithmetic mean, which yields a uniform-stability bound for \mName strictly tighter than the standard bound for SGD. Empirically across generation, classification, and regression at LPM scale, \mName delivers consistent improvements in mean performance and reductions in run-to-run variance over a broad suite of tasks, with no extra training-time or storage cost beyond a single backward pass.

We introduce \textbf{GRAIN} (\textbf{G}roup \textbf{A}ggregation via m\textbf{IN}-norm objective), a lightweight training algorithm that replaces the mean aggregation used in mini-batch optimization (both across mini-batches and within a mini-batch) with a min-norm convex combination of group-wise gradients. \mName guarantees a non-negative inner product between the aggregated update and every group gradient, resolving intra- and inner-batch gradient conflict, and retains an $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ convergence rate comparable to SGD. Under mild smoothness and absolute-continuity assumptions, the min-norm solution differs almost surely from the arithmetic mean, which yields a uniform-stability bound for \mName strictly tighter than the standard bound for SGD. Empirically across generation, classification, and regression at LPM scale, \mName delivers consistent improvements in mean performance and reductions in run-to-run variance over a broad suite of tasks, with no extra training-time or storage cost beyond a single backward pass.

title: Querying of Multi-Version RDF Knowledge Graphs through Condensed Representations
abstract: L'évolution constante des informations du monde réel nécessite des graphes de connaissances dynamiques capables de représenter des ensembles de données multiversionnés. Les systèmes d'archivage traditionnels basés sur le cadre de description des ressources ont du mal à stocker et à interroger efficacement des historiques de versions complexes et non linéaires, tels que ceux comportant des ramifications et des fusions simultanées. Afin de remédier aux limites théoriques et pratiques de la gestion des graphes de connaissances multiversionnés, cette thèse formalise un modèle de « représentation condensée » pour le versionnage RDF. Plutôt que de conserver des copies de données indépendantes ou des chaînes delta séquentielles, le modèle condensé proposé mappe chaque quadruplet RDF unique à un ensemble mathématiquement défini d'instantanés valides, réduisant ainsi la redondance structurelle. Afin de permettre des requêtes temporelles expressives sur ce modèle, cette recherche introduit une nouvelle algèbre de requêtes SPARQL spécialement conçue pour les données condensées. Cette algèbre est prise en charge par un système de types spécialisé qui suit les représentations des variables (en identifiant si les variables sont liées à des termes, des identifiants ou des ensembles d'instantanés condensés) tout au long du cycle de vie de l'exécution. Une contribution théorique centrale de cette thèse est la preuve formelle de l'équivalence entre les modèles d'évaluation plats et condensés. Cette démonstration rigoureuse établit que les évaluations de requêtes sur la représentation condensée préservent une exactitude sémantique stricte, donnant des résultats identiques aux évaluations plates traditionnelles sans nécessiter de coûteux aplatissement des données. Enfin, ce cadre formel est mis en œuvre de manière pratique dans "Concurrent Versioning of knowledge Graphs", un système de bout en bout qui compile l'algèbre SPARQL condensée en SQL pour l'exécuter sur un backend de base de données relationnelle. Des tests de performance expérimentaux ont été réalisés afin de valider l'approche proposée.

title: A Context-Driven Artificial Intelligence Framework for Detecting Fraudulent Activities in Payment Systems
abstract: The expansion of digital payment platforms has created a growing need for robust and reliable fraud detection systems to safeguard financial transactions. Earlier approaches to fraud detection were primarily based on manual verification, rule-driven mechanisms, and simple statistical models. These methods required substantial human involvement, were time-intensive, and struggled to identify sophisticated fraud patterns within large and continuously evolving transaction datasets. As the volume and complexity of digital payments increased, these traditional techniques became inadequate, particularly in supporting real-time decision-making. To address these limitations, this work proposes an intelligent web-based framework for comprehensive fraud detection in Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions by leveraging advanced machine learning and deep learning methodologies. The system is implemented using the Flask framework and incorporates natural language processing techniques to process textual transaction data. For feature representation, Sentence Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (SBERT) is employed to generate contextual embeddings that capture semantic relationships within the data. These embeddings are then used to train and evaluate multiple classification models, including Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB), Bernoulli Naive Bayes (BNB), Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB), and a Histogram-based Gradient Boosting (HGB) classifier. The framework supports both binary classification for fraud identification and multi-class classification for categorizing transaction types. Experimental results demonstrate that the HGB model achieves superior performance, delivering high accuracy along with strong Precision, Recall, and F1-score compared to conventional approaches. Additionally, the system provides a secure web interface that allows users to upload datasets and obtain real-time predictions, with options to download results for further analysis. Overall, the proposed solution enhances automation, scalability, and predictive accuracy, contributing to more effective and efficient fraud detection in digital financial systems.

title: THE STRATEGIC IMPORTANCE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES IN BUSINESS MANAGEMENT AND THEIR IMPACT ON ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT
abstract: The rapid development of digital technologies has significantly changed the modern business environment. Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are becoming one of the most important strategic tools for improving business management systems. This article analyzes the role of artificial intelligence in increasing enterprise efficiency, optimizing decision-making processes, improving marketing strategies, and strengthening competitiveness.

title: Quantum Computing for Construction Robots: Challenges and Opportunities
abstract: Construction robotics play a crucial role in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry, but they face significant computational challenges due to dynamic environments, multi-agent coordination, and largescale combinatorial optimization problems.Quantum computing (QC) offers potential advantages for large-scale search and combinatorial tasks, but its relevance to construction robotics remains unclear.This paper presents a scoping review of QC in robotics.We first collect literature using keyword search from Scopus and Web of Science databases, and then screen through data and include related literature following PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews).We analyze the 96 included studies using bibliometric and thematic analyses to identify research trends and challenges for construction robotics.Results show growing interest in QC robotics since 2020, with dominant applications in path planning, kinematics and control, multi-robot coordination, and decision-making.We identify key barriers to applying QC in construction robotics, including current hardware limitations, simulation-to-real gaps, stringent safety and explainability requirements, and suggest future research directions, including hybrid quantum-classical approaches, QC robotics benchmarks, and explainable QC.

title: Predicting File Types from User Behavior: An Ensemble Learning Approach with Advanced Feature Engineering
abstract: In this article, we describe the first fully reproducible end-to-end machine learning pipeline that predicts the type of files accessed through user file-access logs. In contrast to prior work that relies on raw categorical metadata or manually crafted heuristics, our approach involves integrating multiple complementary modules to support analysis of behavioral log data. Firstly, we extensively engineer domain-aware features (over forty) capturing temporal relationships, structure of paths, application contexts, and filename pattern regularity in human file-access behavior. Secondly, we utilize SMOTE-Tomek to improve minority-class representation within severely imbalanced real-world access logs and remove noisy majority-class boundary points. Thirdly, we apply Optima&s;s Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) to automate hyperparameter optimization for the large parameter space to be explored and reduce the need for manual tuning. Finally, our predictive model consists of a soft-voting ensemble combining a TPE-tuned LightGBM classifier with a Random Forest model to leverage the complementary strengths of boosting and bagging for robust generation of calibrated probability estimates suitable for use in downstream decision making. We evaluate the proposed system using a 20K-instance synthetic dataset generated from carefully designed behavioral patterns; the proposed system demonstrates an accuracy of 81% when compared to other traditional baselines and matches or exceeds many prior file-access prediction methods in the literature. The pipeline is modular, interpretable, reproducible, and designed for practical deployment applications including predictive caching, context-aware file recommendations, and anomaly detection. Diagnostic plots and ablation studies are used to demonstrate the contributions of each module and provide a base for future extension into real-world production logs.

title: Quantum Wiener architecture for quantum reservoir computing
abstract: This work focuses on quantum reservoir computing and, in particular, on quantum Wiener architectures (qWiener), consisting of quantum linear dynamic networks with weak continuous measurements and classical nonlinear static readouts. We provide the first rigorous proof that qWiener systems retain the fading-memory property and universality of classical Wiener architectures, despite quantum constraints on linear dynamics and measurement backaction. Furthermore, we develop a kernel-theoretic interpretation showing that qWiener reservoirs naturally induce deep kernels, providing a principled framework for analyzing their expressivity. We further characterize the simplest qWiener instantiation, consisting of concatenated quantum harmonic oscillators, and show the difference with respect to the classical case. Finally, we empirically evaluate the architecture on standard reservoir computing benchmarks, demonstrating systematic performance gains over prior classical and quantum reservoir computing models.

title: CP-IDC: Consensus prototype-guided incomplete multi-view decoupled clustering
abstract: The goal of multi-view clustering is to integrate information from multiple perspectives to reveal the inherent clustering structure within data. However, real-world data often suffers from missing views. Moreover, existing methods mostly fail to properly handle the inherent coupling between consistency and complementarity information across views, resulting in learned representations lacking sufficient discriminative power. To address this, this paper proposes a consensus prototype-guided incomplete multi-view decoupled clustering method. First, we decouple features across views into consistency representations and complementarity representations, ensuring information separation through dual supervision. Next, a learnable consensus prototype is introduced. Through prototype alignment and contrastive loss, these prototypes drive the consistency representations across all views to converge toward the correct semantic center while diverging from other centers. This achieves robust implicit completion and discriminative clustering at the semantic level. We conduct extensive experiments across eight diverse datasets and compare our approach against ten state-of-the-art incomplete multi-view clustering methods. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for incomplete multi-view clustering.

title: Layer-wise Probing of wav2vec 2.0 and Whisper for Consonant Cluster Reduction in African American English
abstract: Self-supervised and supervised speech models are increasingly used to investigate which linguistic information their internal representations encode, and at what level of abstraction they encode it. One underexplored phenomenon is consonant cluster reduction (CCR) in African American English (AAE), a widespread phonological process and a source of automatic speech recognition (ASR) disparity. To examine how CCR is represented, we conduct speaker-independent layer-wise probing of wav2vec2-base and Whisper-small using two tasks: segmental reduction detection and segmental restoration of underlying cluster identity. Both models distinguish reduced and canonical forms with high accuracy. Crucially, reduced segments retain cues to their underlying stops, indicating that CCR is encoded as structured gradient phonological variation rather than simple segmental deletion. These results demonstrate structured phonological encoding of AAE CCR patterns in modern speech models.

title: From Text Metrics to Model Internals: A Study of Whisper ASR Hallucination Detection
abstract: Hallucinations of ASR models - fluent transcriptions with no basis in audio - degrade system performance and pose risks in downstream applications. Robust detection of such errors remains a challenge. This paper studies Whisper large v3 hallucination detection on real-speech human-annotated data across three paradigms: text-based, LLM-based, and internal decoder state probing. Text classifiers utilizing metrics for text evaluation achieve high recall but degrade without reference transcripts. LLM-based detection improves precision with domain-specific prompt conditioning, yet remains less competitive than the lightweight text-based methods. Probing Whisper's decoder representations, without a ground-truth reference, yields the strongest performance, revealing that hallucination traits are encoded across intermediate decoding layers. A late-fusion meta-classifier combining text and internal-state outputs achieves the best overall detection performance.

title: Can Single-View Mesh Reconstruction Generalize to Robot Camera Rotation?
abstract: Single-view mesh reconstruction predicts object meshes and spatial layouts from a single observation, making it attractive for fast robot spatial reasoning and real-to-sim digital twins. However, robot-mounted cameras naturally rotate during manipulation and navigation, while learned single-view reconstruction models often rely on view-dependent priors and may generalize poorly to out-of-distribution camera rotations. Such rotations can introduce 3D inconsistencies, incorrect layouts, and violations of physical constraints, but this failure mode remains under-evaluated. We introduce an evaluation protocol with controlled axis-wise roll, pitch, and yaw sweeps to trace errors in monocular depth estimation (MDE), canonical object meshes, camera-space layout, and physical plausibility within a representative SAM3D-style pipeline. On the Aria Digital Twin dataset and a real Franka wrist-camera sequence, camera rotations induce MDE distortion, layout drift, and collision penetration, while canonical mesh predictions remain relatively stable. A two-stage SAM3D+FoundationPose pipeline is more robust than one-stage feed-forward layout prediction, and our Gravity-Aware Refinement reduces one-stage pairwise ICP-based layout-orientation error by 47.1%. Our evaluation reveals that current single-view mesh reconstruction methods generalize poorly to robot camera rotation, and suggests that explicit gravity cues are important for reliable robotic single-view mesh reconstruction.

title: AUTOMATIC TRANSCRIPTION AND CLASSIFICATION OF CUSTOMER CALL RECORDINGS FOR CRM ANALYTICS: A WHISPER-BASED WEB SYSTEM
abstract: This paper presents a web-based system that transcribes customer call-centre recordings and classifies them into CRM categories. Audio is stored in a relational database and transcribed into Azerbaijani text with Open AI Whisper; each transcript is then assigned a category by a supervised text classifier. Four classifiers — Multinomial Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and a linear Support Vector Machine (SVM) — are compared on TF-IDF features over 1,480 calls in five categories. The linear SVM performs best (accuracy = 91.2%, macro-F1 = 0.89) and Whisper reaches a 14.8% word error rate (WER) with the large-v3 model. Deployed as a Flask application with sub-50 ms classification latency, the pipeline offers Azerbaijani call centres a low-cost route to automated call analytics.

title: Simulation of Potential Energy Curves for H₂ and LiH Molecules Using the Variational Quantum Eigensolver: A Comparative Study of Ideal and Noisy Quantum Hardware Conditions on Qiskit
abstract: This study investigates the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm that partitions the computational workload between a quantum processing unit and a classical optimiser to determine the ground-state energies of molecular systems. The Qiskit SDK v1.x framework is employed, utilising the PySCFDriver module within the qiskit-nature package to construct second-quantised molecular electronic Hamiltonians for two representative systems: Hydrogen ( ) and Lithium Hydride ( ). For the complete active space is retained without spatial reduction, mapping the full Hamiltonian onto a 4-qubit register. However for the full STO-3G representation demands 12 qubits, rendering direct classical parameter optimisation computationally intractable. This bottleneck is resolved by applying an ActiveSpaceTransformer (num_electrons=2, num_spatial_orbitals=3) to freeze the chemically inactive lithium core electrons, reducing the active register to 6 qubits. Fermionic operators are subsequently converted to Pauli strings via the Jordan-Wigner transformation ( ) enabling the quantum processor to evaluate the molecular Hamiltonian as a circuit while preserving the fermionic anti-commutation relations. Under ideal, noise-free simulation using the StatevectorEstimator primitive paired with the COBYLA optimiser (maxiter=200), all VQE energy points converge precisely onto the Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) classical baseline across the full range of interatomic separations. This confirms that the hardware-efficient TwoLocal ansatz ( rotation layers and entanglement layers with reps=3) possesses sufficient expressive power to capture the molecular ground-state wavefunction. Introducing gate-level noise through AerSimulator backends calibrated from the FakeManilaV2 and FakeNairobiV2 hardware profiles—with optimisation driven by the SPSA algorithm (maxiter=150)—reveals two critical failure modes. A systematic upward energy bias is observed, attributable to depolarising gate errors and measurement readout faults that prevent the optimiser from reaching the true minimum energy eigenvalue. Additionally, severe stochastic oscillations between 1.0 Å and 1.5 Å on the curve induce premature convergence of the SPSA optimiser to spurious local minima. These results demonstrate that unmitigated hardware noise renders VQE incapable of reliably predicting equilibrium bond lengths on current NISQ devices, motivating the future integration of Zero-Noise Extrapolation (ZNE), readout error mitigation, and Virtual Distillation into the computational pipeline. Keywords—Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE); Qiskit 1.x; Potential Energy Curve; Molecular Ground-State Energy; Hardware-Efficient Ansatz; Gate-Level Noise Simulation; ActiveSpaceTransformer; NISQ Devices.

title: The Role Of Artificial Intelligence In Shaping Consumer Trust And Brand Perception In Digital Marketing
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology in digital marketing, enabling organizations to deliver personalized, efficient, and data-driven customer experiences. The increasing use of AI-powered tools such as chatbots, recommendation systems, predictive analytics, and automated customer support has significantly influenced the way consumers interact with brands in the digital environment. As consumer trust and brand perception play a crucial role in determining business success, understanding the impact of AI on these factors has become increasingly important. This study examines the role of Artificial Intelligence in shaping consumer trust and brand perception in digital marketing through a comprehensive review of existing literature and secondary data sources. The research adopts a descriptive and conceptual approach by analyzing scholarly articles, industry reports, and recent studies related to AI applications in marketing. The review identifies key dimensions of AI-driven marketing, including personalization, responsiveness, transparency, and customer engagement, that contribute to improved consumer experiences. The findings indicate that AI technologies positively influence consumer trust by providing relevant recommendations, timely responses, and customized interactions. Enhanced trust subsequently contributes to favorable brand perception, increased customer satisfaction, and stronger brand loyalty. However, concerns regarding data privacy, security, and ethical use of AI continue to influence consumer attitudes toward AI-enabled marketing practices. The study highlights that organizations that adopt transparent and responsible AI strategies are more likely to gain consumer confidence and establish a positive brand image. The study concludes that Artificial Intelligence serves as a strategic tool for strengthening consumer trust and enhancing brand perception in digital marketing. Effective and ethical implementation of AI can help organizations build sustainable customer relationships and achieve long-term competitive advantage in the evolving digital marketplace.

title: Hybrid Batch Training Ratios and Zero-Shot Retrieval Performance in Low-Resource Languages
abstract: Information retrieval across different languages is an increasingly important challenge in natural language processing. Recent approaches based on multilingual pre-trained language models have achieved remarkable success, yet they often optimize for either monolingual, cross-lingual, or multilingual retrieval performance at the expense of others. title: Morgan-Tanglish-v7: Sentence Embeddings for Romanised Tamil-English Code-Mixed Text
abstract: AbstractWe introduce Morgan-Tanglish-v7, a novel 118M-parameter sentence embedding model optimized specifically for Romanised Tamil-English (Tanglish) code-mixed text, addressing a critical gap in contemporary cross-lingual semantic representations. Existing state-of-the-art multilingual and English-centric models—including all-MiniLM-L6-v2, BAAI/bge-m3, and L3Cube-IndicSBERT—demonstrate catastrophic failure modes when evaluating code-switched text, primarily due to their reliance on formal native-script corpora and a lack of exposure to non-standard Latin-script syntactic variations. To resolve the structural and lexical divergence inherent to code-mixed communication, we deliver three major contributions to the open-source NLP ecosystem: 1. Tanglish-Corpus-185k: A highly curated dataset comprising 185,973 domain-diverse sentences. This corpus represents an 11.8x scale expansion over the previous largest benchmark and was engineered via a robust 5-gate morphological filtering pipeline. This framework bypasses standard n-gram language identifiers in favor of a specialized 1,018-token Tamil lexicon and 27 granular grammatical pattern detectors.2. Concept Cluster Training (CCT): A novel algorithmic augmentation technique designed to systematically mitigate the "lexical gap problem." By generating C(n,2) positive pairs from n maximally diverse structural expressions of identical underlying concepts, CCT enforces mathematical invariance between surface-level vocabulary and core semantic intent.3. TanglishSTS Benchmark: The first human-annotated Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) benchmark for Romanised Tamil-English, containing 325 carefully calibrated pairs validated by native speakers. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that Morgan-Tanglish-v7 achieves a Spearman rank correlation coefficient of 0.8689 on TanglishSTS. This significantly outperforms all-MiniLM-L6-v2 by +15.79 points, L3Cube-IndicSBERT by +10.47 points, and the 5x larger BAAI/bge-m3 (570M) model by +11.06 points, establishing a new state-of-the-art for low-resource, code-mixed sentence-level representation learning. All models, data pipelines, evaluation benchmarks, and interactive deployment spaces are publicly accessible at huggingface.co/vishnuexe.

title: A Hybrid Statistical-Machine Learning Framework for Risk-Based Screening of High-Frequency Carbon Emission Data Under Emissions Trading Systems
abstract: Reliable carbon emission data are essential for the effective operation of emissions trading systems (ETS), especially as China’s ETS expands to include energy-intensive industries. This study proposes a hybrid, risk-based anomaly detection framework for high-frequency CO2 emission data by cross-validating material-based emissions with flue gas-based monitoring data. Under normal operating conditions, the ratio of material-based to flue gas-based emissions is expected to remain within a relatively stable distribution. Potential high-risk periods can therefore be identified when this relationship is distorted or when local temporal patterns deviate from expected behavior. The framework combines Hartigan’s dip test with a window-based Random Forest (RF) classifier, which is suitable for continuous monitoring data that may exhibit temporal dependence. The framework was evaluated using 15-min CO2 emission data from a cement production facility, with simulations of anomaly magnitude, duration, and mode. Results show that the dip test performs well for long-lasting or strong anomalies, whereas the RF model is more sensitive to subtle, short-term deviations. In the integrated framework, 94.7% of anomalous periods were detected by at least one method and flagged as potential data-quality risks, whereas normal periods were not flagged, supporting its use to prioritize verification efforts.

title: APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN ERGONOMICS: SENTIMENT ANALYSIS REGARDING THE WORK ENVIRONMENT
abstract: This article contextualizes Quality of Life at Work and the use of Artificial Intelligence, specifically the Naive Bayes algorithm, for sentiment analysis based on testimonials from workers about the company in which they work or have worked. Some areas of application for Naive Bayes are presented, as well as its application to support the analysis of textual comments, with the objective of capturing the worker's perception of the environment in which they are inserted. A small group of comments made on Glassdoor.com.br was used for the analysis, making it possible to observe an accuracy of 75% in the probabilistic responses obtained through the algorithm. The following labels are returned for the analyzed text: joy or fear, meaning joy as satisfaction with the environment and fear as dissatisfaction or discomfort with the environment. Consequently, a greater or lesser Quality of Life at Work can be inferred through the use of Artificial Intelligence.

title: Recursive QLSTM with Dynamic Variational Quantum Circuit Adaptation
abstract: Recent advances in quantum computing and machine learning have motivated the development of quantum models for sequential data processing. In this paper, we propose a Recursive Quantum Long Short-Term Memory model, or Recursive QLSTM, which extends QLSTM through metacore-based recursive constructions. We numerically test the model under different input sequence lengths, metacore designs, and recursive rules, and identify the best-performing architecture among these variants. For this selected model, we further provide theoretical arguments explaining why its recursive structure improves temporal information propagation and enhances learning performance. Our results suggest that Recursive QLSTM offers a flexible and effective framework for quantum recurrent learning over input time series of various lengths.
